agent: one subagent, 100/100 probes spent, 13 rules + fallback, tools covered 5/21
verdict_vs_sgd_same_budget: the deduced rule beats SGD at the same 100-query budget on labels (0.8701 vs 0.8639)

hybrid.gate: override the head where its top-2 logit margin <= 0.75
hybrid.reading: the gate is not what helps; the rule's direction does. Same gate with a random tool choice scores BELOW the incumbent.

exact_weight_compile.status: my analytic 2-layer construction is wrong -- not an architectural limit
exact_weight_compile.correction: I first wrote 'one hidden layer cannot express an AND of thresholds'. The next measurement refuted that: distilling the rule INTO the shipped 42x192x21 shape reproduces it at 0.9978 rule-agreement when trained on all 3,719 rule labels. So the shape holds the rule fine; the analytic closed-form construction is the bug.

learnability_at_budget.reading: expressible in the head shape, but NOT recoverable into it at the 100-query budget -- that is the real limit.

rule_ceiling.reading: the deduced rule is a 0.87-class predictor; its value was never standing alone, it was carrying information the head lacks in the head's own low-margin region.

honest_summary: At 100 queries, a hand-deduced symbolic rule beat SGD on labels (0.8701 vs 0.8639) and, gated to the head's low-margin rows, beat the incumbent (0.9083 vs 0.9043, 25 rescued / 10 broken, p=0.0167) where a random override at the same gate scored 0.8855 -- so the direction, not the gating, is the gain. It did NOT reach the incumbent alone, it covers 5 of 21 tools because 100 probes cannot find the rare classes, and my closed-form weight compile is broken (3,719 mismatches).
